Exercise: Prone Manual Hamstring

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
static

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- extension_of_the_knee_joint
- flexion

Primary Muscles:

- hamstrings

Secondary Muscles:
None

Equipment:
None

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.8

Energy Requirement:
low to moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- hamstring_strength_and_endurance
- neural_activation_of_the_hamstrings

Contraindications:

- Recent hamstring injury or surgery

Exercise Variations:

- name: Partner Resistance with Different Angles, description: Perform the exercise while your partner changes their hand position on your heel, varying angles to target different parts of the hamstrings.
- name: Single-Leg Variation, description: Perform the exercise using one leg at a time for increased challenge and isolation.

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Seated Hamstring Curls, equipment: cable machine
- exercise_name: Romanian Deadlifts, equipment: barbell or dumbbells

Instructions:

- You will need a partner for this exercise. Lay face down with your legs straight. Your assistant will place their hand on your heel.
- To begin, flex the knee to curl your leg up. Your partner should provide resistance, starting light and increasing the pressure as the movement is completed. Communicate with your partner to monitor appropriate resistance levels.
- Pause at the top, returning the leg to the starting position as your partner provides resistance going the other direction.
